core_obligations: Verify that S = A setminus union of the p_i is a multiplicative subset containing 1 (proof lines 7720-7722).
Use the description of Spec(S^{-1}A) and the avoidance lemma to conclude that the primes of S^{-1}A correspond to the primes of A contained in one of the p_i (proof lines 7722-7728).

Deduce that the maximal ideals of S^{-1}A correspond bijectively to the maximal elements (with respect to inclusion) of the finite set of primes, so that the ring is semi-local (proof lines 7729-7731).
proof_roadmap: Check that the complement of the union is multiplicative.
Identify the maximal ideals with the maximal elements.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the localization of a ring at the multiplicative set complementary to a finite union of primes: it shows that set is multiplicative and that the resulting ring is semi-local with maximal ideals in bijection with the maximal elements of the given finite set of primes. The proof checks multiplicativity directly, uses the description of the spectrum of a localization together with the avoidance lemma to see that the primes of S^{-1}A correspond to the primes of A contained in one of the p_i, and reads off the maximal ideals as the maximal elements of the finite set (proof lines 7720-7731). H2: the two-step description of the prime spectrum after localization is the substance.
